mainTopic: The בכור's double portion, why the בכורה went to יוסף, and the count of יעקב's family
overview: This amud opens in the middle of a ברייתא about how big the בכור's double portion (פי שנים) is. Logic alone could argue either for 'double what one brother gets' or for 'double the whole estate.' A פסוק settles it: the בכור gets double what one brother gets. The ברייתא backs this up with פסוקים about ראובן's בכורה passing to יוסף, who received two full shares through אפרים and מנשה. The גמרא then explains why each extra פסוק was needed. Next, רבי חלבו asks why יעקב gave the בכורה specifically to יוסף. The answer, from רבי יונתן, is that it belonged to רחל's line: לאה won it through tearful prayer, and רחל earned it back through her modesty in giving her secret signs to לאה. The amud ends with a question about why יעקב's family is counted as seventy but the list of names shows only sixty-nine, and that discussion continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Logic says: double what one brother gets
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא compares a בכור with one brother to a בכור with five brothers. It argues that in both cases he gets double what one brother gets.
steps.simpleTranslation: Sometimes the בכור splits with one brother, and sometimes with five brothers. With one brother, he gets twice what that one brother gets. So with five brothers too, he should get twice what one brother gets.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא, already in the middle of its discussion, offers a logical argument that the בכור's פי שנים means 'double one brother's share.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: With only one other brother, both readings give the same result, so that case is clear. The ברייתא uses that clear case as the model and stretches it to the case of five brothers. In that bigger case, 'double one brother' gives the בכור 2/7 of the estate.

keyTerms.meaning: like one (double what one brother gets)

steps.confusionAlert: With just one other brother, 'double of one brother' and 'double of all the brothers' come out exactly the same. The disagreement only shows up when there are more brothers.

phrases.english: His portion with one brother,
and his portion with five brothers;
just as his portion with one brother
is double what one brother gets,
so too his portion with five brothers
is double what one brother gets!

steps.triggerLanguage: מָה חֶלְקוֹ עִם אֶחָד פִּי שְׁנַיִם כְּאֶחָד
steps.raayaObject: That פי שנים means double what one brother gets
steps.raayaSupportSource: A logical comparison to the simple case of a בכור with one brother

steps.title: The same logic can argue: double the whole estate
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא turns the comparison around. It shows that the same model could prove the בכור gets double of everything the other brothers get.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or go the other way: with one brother, the בכור gets double of all the property, meaning twice what everyone else gets together. So with five brothers too, he should get double of all the property.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא shows that the logic from step 1 can be flipped to reach the opposite answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The case of one brother can be described in two ways: 'double one brother' or 'double all the other heirs.' Whichever description you choose decides how you apply it to five brothers. Because the logic works either way, it cannot prove anything by itself.

keyTerms.meaning: or go this way (try the opposite reasoning)
of all the property (double the rest of the estate combined)

phrases.english: Or go this way:

phrases.aramaic: חֶלְקוֹ עִם אֶחָד, וְחֶלְקוֹ עִם חֲמִשָּׁה;
phrases.english: his portion with one brother, and his portion with five brothers;
just as his portion with one brother
is double of all the property,
phrases.notes: Twice as much as all the other brothers together. With five brothers, that would be 2/3 of the estate.

phrases.english: so too his portion with five brothers
is double of all the property!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Neutralizes the logical proof of step 1 by building an equally strong opposite comparison
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects relying on logic alone to decide the question
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The model case of one brother fits both readings, so it cannot pick between them

steps.title: A פסוק decides: double what one brother gets
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא brings a פסוק showing that the inheritance depends on the number of brothers. So the first reasoning (double of one brother) is correct.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says: 'And it shall be, on the day he gives his sons their inheritance.' The תורה made the inheritance grow with the number of brothers. So you should not reason like the second way, but like the first way.
steps.whatsHappening: Since logic could go either way, the ברייתא settles the question with a פסוק and picks the first reasoning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase 'on the day he gives his sons their inheritance' is read as teaching that the brothers' share gets bigger the more brothers there are. That only works if the בכור's portion is measured against one brother, not against the whole estate. So the second reasoning is rejected and 'double one brother' wins.

keyTerms.meaning: like the first version (the first reasoning)

steps.whatToRemember: The בכור's פי שנים is double what one other brother gets, not double the whole estate. Logic was not enough to decide this, so the פסוק settled it.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the practical halacha of how a בכור's share is calculated whenever there are several brothers.

phrases.aramaic: תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: ״וְהָיָה בְּיוֹם הַנְחִילוֹ אֶת בָּנָיו״ –
phrases.english: The verse teaches: 'And it shall be, on the day he gives his sons their inheritance':
phrases.notes: דברים 21:16

phrases.english: the Torah increased the inheritance for the brothers;
phrases.notes: Meaning: the more brothers there are, the more of the estate goes to them.

phrases.aramaic: הָא אֵין עָלֶיךָ לָדוּן כַּלָּשׁוֹן הָאַחֲרוֹן,
phrases.english: so you should not reason like the last version,
phrases.notes: The 'last version' is the second reasoning: double the whole estate.

phrases.english: but like the first version.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: ״וְהָיָה בְּיוֹם הַנְחִילוֹ אֶת בָּנָיו״
steps.raayaObject: That פי שנים means double what one brother gets
steps.raayaSupportSource: דברים 21:16, 'on the day he gives his sons their inheritance'
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Reason like the first version: double what one brother gets

steps.title: More proof from the פסוקים about ראובן and יוסף
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא adds two פסוקים saying that ראובן's בכורה was given to יוסף. This sets up a further proof that step 5 completes.
steps.simpleTranslation: It also says: 'The sons of ראובן, the firstborn of Israel, for he was the firstborn; but because he defiled his father's bed, his birthright was given to the sons of יוסף son of Israel, and not to be counted as firstborn.' And it says: 'For יהודה became strong among his brothers, and a leader came from him, but the birthright went to יוסף.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא brings more פסוקים to back up its answer. This step only sets up the proof; step 5 shows how these פסוקים prove the point.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These פסוקים say that the בכורה, the firstborn's special share, moved from ראובן to יוסף. The ברייתא will use what יוסף actually received to show what a double portion looks like. The sentence ends with a dash, so the argument is not finished yet.

keyTerms.meaning: and it also says (bringing another פסוק)
the birthright, the firstborn's special share
to be counted in the family records

phrases.english: And it says: 'And the sons of Reuben, the firstborn of Israel,
phrases.notes: דברי הימים א 5:1

phrases.english: for he was the firstborn,
but because he defiled his father's bed,

phrases.aramaic: נִתְּנָה בְּכֹרָתוֹ לִבְנֵי יוֹסֵף בֶּן יִשְׂרָאֵל,
phrases.english: his birthright was given to the sons of Joseph, son of Israel,
and not to be counted as the firstborn';
and it says: 'For Judah grew strong among his brothers,
phrases.notes: דברי הימים א 5:2

phrases.english: and the leader came from him,
but the birthright was Joseph's'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds further פסוקים to strengthen the conclusion of step 3
steps.raayaObject: That פי שנים means double what one brother gets
steps.raayaSupportSource: דברי הימים א 5:1-2, ראובן's בכורה given to יוסף (the proof is completed in the next lines)

steps.title: The same word for יוסף and for all generations
steps.stepSummary: A גזירה שוה links the בכורה of יוסף to the בכורה of every future בכור. Both mean a double share like one brother.
steps.simpleTranslation: The word 'birthright' is used about יוסף, and the word 'birthright' is used for all later generations. Just as יוסף's birthright was double the share of one brother, so too the birthright for all generations is double the share of one brother.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא finishes the proof it set up in step 4. It links the word בכורה said about יוסף to the word בכורה in the law of the בכור.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We know what יוסף's בכורה looked like: he got two portions, each the size of one brother's share. Because the same word is used for every בכור, we learn that every בכור also gets double what one brother gets, and not double the whole estate.

keyTerms.meaning: Birthright, the special status and extra share of the firstborn
For all later generations, meaning the general law
Double, measured as twice the share of one brother
Learning one case from another because the same word appears in both

steps.whatToRemember: The בכור gets twice what one brother gets, just as יוסף received two portions.
steps.whyThisMatters: This settles the question from steps 1-3. It decides how the בכור's share is actually calculated.

phrases.english: "Birthright" is said about Joseph,
and "birthright" is said for the later generations;
phrases.notes: This is the word הבכרה in the law of the בכור, דברים 21:17.

phrases.english: just as the birthright said about Joseph
is double, measured like one brother's share,
so too the birthright said for later generations
is double, measured like one brother's share.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the proof begun in step 4 with the פסוקים about יוסף.
steps.raayaObject: The בכור gets double the share of one brother.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A גזירה שוה on the word בכורה, used for יוסף and in דברים 21:17.

steps.title: יעקב gives יוסף one portion above his brothers
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא quotes יעקב's words to יוסף: 'I have given you one portion above your brothers.'
steps.simpleTranslation: And the פסוק says: 'And I have given you one portion above your brothers, which I took from the hand of the Amorite with my sword and with my bow.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא adds another פסוק showing that יוסף got one extra portion more than his brothers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'One portion above your brothers' shows that יוסף's extra share was one more portion, the size of a brother's share. This fits the rule that the בכורה is double like one brother.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And it says', bringing an additional פסוק
The Amorite, one of the nations of כנען

phrases.english: And it says:

phrases.aramaic: ״וַאֲנִי נָתַתִּי לְךָ שְׁכֶם אַחַד עַל אַחֶיךָ,
phrases.english: "And I have given you one portion above your brothers,
phrases.notes: בראשית 48:22

phrases.english: which I took from the hand of the Amorite
with my sword and with my bow"

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאוֹמֵר: ״וַאֲנִי נָתַתִּי לְךָ שְׁכֶם אַחַד עַל אַחֶיךָ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a further פסוק supporting the conclusion of step 5.
steps.raayaObject: יוסף's extra share was one portion more than a brother's.

steps.title: Did יעקב really fight with a sword and bow?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא questions the wording of the פסוק, since another פסוק says we do not rely on our sword and bow.
steps.simpleTranslation: But did he really take it with his sword and his bow? Isn't it already said: 'For I do not trust in my bow, and my sword will not save me'?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא pauses on the words 'my sword and my bow' and points out that they seem to clash with a פסוק in תהלים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: תהלים says a person should not trust his own weapons. So it seems strange for יעקב to say he won with his sword and bow. This sets up the explanation in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: 'But is it really so?', a rhetorical challenge
'But isn't it already said?', pointing to a clashing פסוק

phrases.english: But did he really take it with his sword and his bow?!
But isn't it already said:
"For I do not trust in my bow,
phrases.notes: תהלים 44:7

phrases.english: and my sword will not save me"!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the plain meaning of the פסוק quoted in step 6.
steps.kashyaTarget: The words 'with my sword and with my bow' in בראשית 48:22.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: תהלים 44:7 says one does not trust in sword and bow, so יעקב could not mean real weapons.

steps.title: Sword means prayer, bow means pleading
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא explains that יעקב's 'sword' and 'bow' were really prayer and pleading.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, 'my sword' means prayer, and 'my bow' means pleading.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers the question by reading the weapons as a picture: יעקב's real tools were prayer and pleading to ה׳.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the words are read this way, the two פסוקים no longer clash. יעקב won through prayer, not by trusting his weapons.

phrases.english: Rather, "my sword" means prayer,
"my bow" means pleading.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the contradiction raised in step 7.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: יעקב meant real weapons, which clashes with תהלים.
steps.terutzMaskana: Sword and bow are a picture of prayer and pleading, so there is no clash.

steps.title: Why did the ברייתא need more proofs?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the ברייתא kept adding פסוקים with 'and it says'.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why does the ברייתא say 'and it says' and bring more proofs?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now looks back at the whole ברייתא. It asks why the first proof was not enough. This question sets up the answer in the next steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Usually a ברייתא adds 'and it says' only when the earlier proof has a weakness. The גמרא wants to know what that weakness is.

phrases.english: What is the point of "and it says"?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Steps out of the ברייתא to analyze its structure.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the ברייתא needed extra proofs beyond the first פסוק.

steps.title: The first פסוק may teach רבי יוחנן בן ברוקא's rule
steps.stepSummary: The first פסוק could be used for a different law, so the ברייתא brings 'And the sons of ראובן the firstborn of ישראל'.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you would say that the first פסוק comes to teach the rule of רבי יוחנן בן ברוקא, come and hear: 'And the sons of ראובן, the firstborn of ישראל'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the first weakness. The פסוק from step 3 might be needed for a different teaching, so a new proof is brought.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the פסוק from step 3 teaches רבי יוחנן בן ברוקא's law, it cannot also prove how the בכור's share is measured. So the ברייתא brings the פסוק showing that ראובן's בכורה went to יוסף, as quoted in step 4.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And if you would say', bringing up a possible objection
A תנא with his own rule about how a father divides his property

phrases.english: And if you would say

phrases.aramaic: הַאי לְכִדְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בֶּן בְּרוֹקָא הוּא דַּאֲתָא –
phrases.english: that this verse comes to teach the rule of Rabbi Yoḥanan ben Beroka,
phrases.notes: This is the פסוק from step 3. He holds that a father may give his property to whichever son he chooses.

phrases.english: come and hear:
"And the sons of Reuben, the firstborn of Israel."
phrases.notes: דברי הימים א 5:1. The פסוק goes on to say his birthright was given to יוסף's sons.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי תֵּימָא הַאי לְכִדְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בֶּן בְּרוֹקָא הוּא דַּאֲתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 9 by pointing out the weakness in the first proof.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The first פסוק might teach רבי יוחנן בן ברוקא's rule, so the ברייתא adds the פסוק about ראובן's בכורה going to יוסף.

steps.title: An exact word match: 'and the birthright was יוסף's'
steps.stepSummary: 'His birthright' is not the exact same word as 'birthright', so the ברייתא brings 'and the birthright was יוסף's'.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you would say that we do not learn 'birthright' from 'his birthright', come and hear: 'And the birthright was יוסף's.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the second weakness. The word in the ראובן פסוק is slightly different, so the ברייתא brings a פסוק with the exact matching word.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A גזירה שוה works best when the words match exactly. בכורתו ('his birthright') is not the same as בכורה. The פסוק 'והבכורה ליוסף' uses the exact word, so the link to the law of the בכור holds firm.

keyTerms.meaning: We do not learn one from the other

steps.whatToRemember: Every 'and it says' in the ברייתא fixes a weakness in the proof before it. The next steps finish the chain by proving that יוסף's share was really double.

phrases.english: And if you would say
that we do not learn "birthright" from "his birthright,"
come and hear: "And the birthright was Joseph's."
phrases.notes: דברי הימים א 5:2

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers a weakness in the proof brought in step 10.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'His birthright' may not match 'birthright', so the ברייתא brings 'והבכורה ליוסף', which uses the exact word.

steps.title: Proving that יוסף's share was double
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains the next פסוק in the ברייתא. It is there to prove that יוסף got a double portion, like one brother counted twice.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you would say: how do we know that יוסף himself got double the share of one brother? Come and hear: 'And I have given you one portion above your brothers.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא continues explaining why the ברייתא kept adding פסוקים. This פסוק shows that יוסף got one extra portion more than each of his brothers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 11 proved that the בכורה went to יוסף. Someone could still ask whether יוסף actually received a double share. The words 'one portion above your brothers' answer this, because they show יוסף got one portion more than each other son.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you would say (brings up a possible objection)
A double portion, the share a בכור inherits

phrases.english: And if you would say:
Regarding יוסף himself –
from where do we know that he got double the share of one brother?
Come and hear:

phrases.aramaic: ״וַאֲנִי נָתַתִּי לְךָ שְׁכֶם אַחַד עַל אַחֶיךָ״.
phrases.english: "And I have given you one portion above your brothers."
phrases.notes: בראשית 48:22

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the chain of answers explaining why each added פסוק in the ברייתא is needed.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the ברייתא needed yet another פסוק.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: To prove that יוסף's portion was a true double share, using 'שכם אחד על אחיך'.

steps.title: Maybe the extra portion was just a palm tree
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא challenges the proof. Maybe 'one portion' was only a small extra gift, like a single palm tree.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said to אביי: Say that it means just a palm tree!
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא attacks the proof from the last step. He suggests the 'extra portion' might have been only a small present and not a full share.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'portion' does not say how big the portion was. If it was only a palm tree, the פסוק would not prove that יוסף got a full double share.

phrases.english: רב פפא said to אביי:
Say it means just a palm tree!
phrases.notes: In other words, maybe the 'one portion' was just a small extra gift, not a whole equal share.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the proof brought in step 12.
steps.kashyaTarget: The proof from 'שכם אחד על אחיך' that יוסף got a full double share.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: 'Portion' could mean a small gift, like a palm tree, so the size of the share is not proven.

steps.title: אפרים and מנשה count like ראובן and שמעון
steps.stepSummary: אביי answers with a פסוק showing that יוסף's two sons each got a full tribal share.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: For your question the פסוק says: 'אפרים and מנשה shall be mine just like ראובן and שמעון.'
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers רב פפא's challenge. He brings a פסוק showing that יוסף received two full shares.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אפרים and מנשה are compared to ראובן and שמעון, who are two full brothers. So יוסף's family received two complete portions and not a small extra gift. This proves the double portion was a real full share.

keyTerms.meaning: The פסוק speaks to your exact question

steps.whatToRemember: יוסף received the בכורה as a full double share, because his two sons each count as a full tribe like ראובן and שמעון.

phrases.english: He said to him: about you the verse says:
"אפרים and מנשה –
like ראובן and שמעון they shall be mine."
phrases.notes: בראשית 48:5

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב פפא's challenge from step 13.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Brings an additional פסוק that settles the size of the share.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The 'one portion' might have been only a small gift like a palm tree.
steps.terutzMaskana: אפרים and מנשה each equal a full brother, so יוסף had two full shares.

steps.title: Why did יעקב move the בכורה from ראובן to יוסף?
steps.stepSummary: רבי חלבו asks רבי שמואל בר נחמני what reason יעקב had for taking the בכורה from ראובן and giving it to יוסף.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חלבו asked רבי שמואל בר נחמני: What did יעקב see that he took the בכורה from ראובן and gave it to יוסף?
steps.whatsHappening: A new discussion begins here. רבי חלבו asks for the reason behind יעקב's choice.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question has two parts: why take the בכורה away from ראובן, and why give it to יוסף. The גמרא will soon show that only the second part is a real question.

keyTerms.meaning: What did he see, meaning what was his reason

phrases.aramaic: בְּעָא מִינֵּיהּ רַבִּי חֶלְבּוֹ מֵרַבִּי שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר נַחְמָנִי:
phrases.english: רבי חלבו asked רבי שמואל בר נחמני:
What did יעקב see
that he took the בכורה from ראובן,
and gave it to יוסף?

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּעָא מִינֵּיהּ רַבִּי חֶלְבּוֹ מֵרַבִּי שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר נַחְמָנִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic about the reason for transferring the בכורה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: יעקב's reason for taking the בכורה from ראובן and giving it to יוסף.

steps.title: The reason for taking it from ראובן is written in the פסוק
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא wonders about the question: the פסוק already says ראובן lost the בכורה because he defiled his father's bed.
steps.simpleTranslation: What did he see?! It is written: 'And because he defiled his father's bed.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי חלבו's question. The reason ראובן lost the בכורה is already written in the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is no need to ask why ראובן lost the בכורה, because דברי הימים says it openly. So the first half of the question seems to make no sense.

phrases.english: What did he see?!
"And because he defiled his father's bed" is written!
phrases.notes: דברי הימים א 5:1

steps.triggerLanguage: מָה רָאָה?! וּבְחַלְּלוֹ יְצוּעֵי אָבִיו כְּתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the wording of רבי חלבו's question.
steps.kashyaTarget: The part of the question asking why the בכורה was taken from ראובן.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A פסוק already states the reason openly, so there is nothing to ask.

steps.title: The real question: why יוסף in particular
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that רבי חלבו was really asking why the בכורה went specifically to יוסף.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, what did he see that he gave it to יוסף?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא makes the question narrower. The real question is why יוסף was the one chosen.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Losing the בכורה is explained by ראובן's sin. That sin does not explain why the בכורה went to יוסף instead of another brother, so that is the real question.

phrases.english: Rather, what did he see that he gave it to יוסף?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves step 16 by narrowing the question.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterprets the question as asking only about the choice of יוסף.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The question was about why ראובן lost the בכורה.
steps.terutzMaskana: The question is why the בכורה was given specifically to יוסף.

steps.title: The משל of the orphan who repays the homeowner
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמואל בר נחמני answers with a משל: an orphan raised by a homeowner becomes rich and wants to benefit him.
steps.simpleTranslation: I will tell you a parable. What is this like? Like a homeowner who raised an orphan in his house. Later that orphan became rich and said: I will give the homeowner benefit from my property.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי שמואל בר נחמני answers why יוסף was chosen. He uses a משל about repaying kindness.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משל, the one who received kindness wants to pay it back. The point is that יעקב gave the בכורה to יוסף as repayment, because יוסף provided for יעקב in מצרים.
steps.confusionAlert: Be careful about who plays which role. In the משל it is the orphan who repays the homeowner, while in real life יעקב repays יוסף. The idea being compared is simply paying back someone who supported you.

phrases.english: I will tell you a parable,
phrases.notes: Now רבי שמואל בר נחמני is answering רבי חלבו.

phrases.english: what is the matter like?

phrases.aramaic: לְבַעַל הַבַּיִת שֶׁגִּדֵּל יָתוֹם בְּתוֹךְ בֵּיתוֹ;
phrases.english: Like a homeowner who raised an orphan in his house;
after some time that orphan became rich,
and said: I will give the homeowner benefit from my property.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶמְשׁוֹל לְךָ מָשָׁל, לְמָה הַדָּבָר דּוֹמֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the narrowed question from step 17.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: יעקב gave the בכורה to יוסף to repay him for his kindness, just as a grateful person repays someone who supported him.

steps.title: Would יוסף get nothing without ראובן's sin?
steps.stepSummary: רבי חלבו challenges the answer: if repaying יוסף was the reason, would יעקב have given him nothing had ראובן not sinned?
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: And if ראובן had not sinned, would יעקב not have given יוסף any benefit at all?!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי חלבו pushes back on the משל. Repaying יוסף should not depend on ראובן happening to sin.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If gratitude was the reason, יעקב would want to repay יוסף no matter what. But in the actual story, יוסף received the בכורה only because ראובן lost it, so gratitude alone does not explain the choice.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: וְאִי לָאו דַּחֲטָא רְאוּבֵן,
phrases.english: He said to him: And if ראובן had not sinned,
phrases.notes: This is רבי חלבו questioning the answer he was just given.

phrases.aramaic: לָא מְהַנֵּי לֵיהּ לְיוֹסֵף וְלָא מִדָּעַם?!
phrases.english: would he not have given יוסף any benefit at all?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the משל answer given in step 18.
steps.kashyaTarget: The explanation that the בכורה was given to יוסף as repayment for his kindness.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A debt of gratitude does not depend on someone else's sin. Since יוסף got the בכורה only because ראובן sinned, gratitude cannot be the full reason.

steps.title: רבי יונתן's reason: the בכורה belonged to רחל and was returned to her
steps.stepSummary: רבי חלבו quotes רבי יונתן: the בכורה was meant for רחל's son. לאה took it through prayer, and because of רחל's modesty, the Holy One gave it back to her.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, didn't your teacher רבי יונתן say this: the בכורה was fit to come from רחל, as it says, 'These are the generations of יעקב: יוסף.' But לאה got ahead of her with prayers for mercy. And because of the modesty רחל had, the Holy One gave it back to her.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי חלבו sets aside the orphan משל and offers a better reason, in the name of רבי שמואל בר נחמני's own teacher, רבי יונתן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משל made it sound like יוסף got the בכורה only by chance, because ראובן happened to sin. רבי יונתן's reason is different: the בכורה always belonged to רחל's line. לאה's prayers took it for a while, and רחל's modesty earned it back. That fully answers why it went specifically to יוסף.

keyTerms.meaning: Mercy, here meaning prayers asking for mercy

steps.whyThisMatters: This becomes the main answer to רבי חלבו's question, and the rest of the piece explains its two parts.

phrases.english: Rather, Rabbi Yonatan, your teacher,
didn't he say this:
The firstborn status was fit to come out from Rachel,
as it is written: "These are the generations of Jacob: Joseph,"
phrases.notes: בראשית 37:2. The פסוק names יוסף as יעקב's main offspring.

phrases.english: but Leah got ahead of her with prayers for mercy;
and because of the modesty that Rachel had,
the Holy One, Blessed be He, gave it back to her.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא רַבִּי יוֹנָתָן רַבָּךְ לֹא כָּךְ אָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After challenging the משל in Step 19, רבי חלבו replaces it with רבי יונתן's explanation.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The בכורה was meant for רחל. לאה took it through prayer, and רחל's modesty brought it back to her son יוסף.

steps.title: What does it mean that לאה got ahead through prayer?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what 'לאה got ahead with mercy' means, and points to the פסוק 'ועיני לאה רכות.'
steps.simpleTranslation: What does 'לאה got ahead of her with mercy' mean? As it is written: 'And לאה's eyes were soft.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא stops to explain one phrase from רבי יונתן's teaching. It quotes a פסוק about לאה's eyes as the hint, which sets up the next question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The source for לאה's prayers is the description of her eyes as 'רכות.' But the meaning of that word is not clear yet. So this step opens a short discussion about what the word means.

phrases.english: What is "Leah got ahead of her with mercy"?
As it is written: "And Leah's eyes were soft"
phrases.notes: בראשית 29:17

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains a phrase from רבי יונתן's statement in Step 20.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What the phrase 'לאה got ahead with mercy' refers to.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: It is connected to the פסוק 'ועיני לאה רכות.'

steps.title: 'Soft eyes' can't be an insult, since the תורה avoids insulting even an animal
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what 'רכות' means. It rejects the plain meaning of 'weak eyes' as an insult: the תורה avoids even calling an animal 'impure,' so it would not insult a righteous woman.
steps.simpleTranslation: What does 'רכות' mean? If you say her eyes were literally weak, is that possible? The פסוק did not speak badly even of an impure animal, as it is written: 'From the pure animal and from the animal that is not pure.' Would it then speak badly of the righteous?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the simple reading of 'רכות,' saying it would be an insult to לאה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof works from small to big. With the animals in the תיבה, the תורה used extra words ('not pure') just to avoid the harsh word 'impure.' If it is that careful about an animal, it surely would not call a צדקת's eyes weak as an insult.

phrases.english: What does "soft" mean?
If you say literally weak,
is that possible? About the disgrace of an impure animal
phrases.notes: אֶפְשָׁר here means 'Is that possible?!' Pause after it, then a new sentence starts.

phrases.english: the verse did not speak,
as it is written: "From the pure animal
and from the animal that is not pure";
phrases.notes: בראשית 7:8. Notice it says 'not pure' instead of just 'impure.'

phrases.english: would the verse speak of the disgrace of the righteous?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the meaning of the word in the פסוק quoted in Step 21.
steps.kashyaTarget: Reading 'רכות' as plainly weak, unattractive eyes
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The תורה avoids insulting even an impure animal, so it surely would not insult a righteous woman.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר: her gifts were long-lasting
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר reads 'רכות' as a hint to 'ארוכות': לאה's gifts lasted a long time.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבי אלעזר said: it means that her gifts were long-lasting.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר answers the challenge by reading 'רכות' as a wordplay instead of a description of her eyes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With this reading, the פסוק praises לאה and does not describe weak eyes at all. Notice that this reading does not mention prayer. So it is a side explanation of the word, and רב's reading next is the one that connects to 'getting ahead with mercy.'

phrases.english: Rather, Rabbi Elazar said:
that her gifts were long-lasting.
phrases.notes: A play on words: רַכּוֹת sounds like אֲרוּכּוֹת, 'long.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 22 by reading the word differently.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpretation of the word through wordplay
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'רכות' means weak eyes, which would be an insult.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'רכות' hints to 'ארוכות': her gifts were long-lasting.

steps.title: רב: her eyes really were weak, and that is praise
steps.stepSummary: רב keeps the plain meaning but says it is praise. לאה heard people saying the older daughter of לבן would marry the older son of רבקה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב said: her eyes really were weak, and it is not a disgrace but a praise for her. She used to hear people at the crossroads saying: רבקה has two sons and לבן has two daughters, the older for the older and the younger for the younger.
steps.whatsHappening: רב gives a different answer to the challenge. He keeps the simple meaning of 'weak eyes' and begins explaining why it is actually praise.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אלעזר changed the meaning of the word. רב keeps the word as it is and changes how we see it: the weakness had a righteous cause. The story starts with the plan everyone talked about, which meant לאה, the older daughter, was set to marry עשו, the older son.

keyTerms.meaning: Really, in truth (keeping the original reading)
The older one for the older one

phrases.english: Rav said:
Really, they were literally weak,
and it is not a disgrace for her,
but rather it is a praise for her.
For she would hear at the crossroads
people who were saying:
Rebecca has two sons,
Laban has two daughters,
the older for the older and the younger for the younger.
phrases.notes: He means the older daughter would marry the older son, and the younger daughter the younger son.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second answer to the challenge of Step 22, disagreeing with רבי אלעזר's approach in Step 23.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Keeps the plain meaning but shows it is not an insult
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Weak eyes would be an insult to a righteous woman.
steps.terutzMaskana: The weak eyes are praise, because of the reason behind them.

steps.title: לאה cried over marrying עשו until her eyelashes fell out
steps.stepSummary: לאה asked about the two sons, learned that the older one was a wicked robber and the younger a quiet man of tents, and cried until her eyelashes fell out.
steps.simpleTranslation: She would sit at the crossroads and ask: The older one, what does he do? He is an evil man who robs people. The younger one, what does he do? 'A quiet man, sitting in tents.' And she would cry until her eyelashes fell out.
steps.whatsHappening: רב finishes his explanation. לאה's eyes became weak from crying and praying not to marry the wicked עשו.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the praise: the weakness came from her fear of marrying a wicked man. Her crying is the 'mercy' (prayer) that רבי יונתן said let לאה get ahead of רחל. That is how her prayers earned her יעקב, and with him the בכורה at first.

keyTerms.meaning: A quiet (wholesome) man sitting in tents

steps.whatToRemember: The בכורה belonged to רחל. לאה's tearful prayers (her 'weak eyes') won it for her firstborn, and רחל's modesty brought it back to יוסף.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't read 'weak eyes' as a criticism of לאה. According to רב, it is a sign of her righteousness and her prayer.

phrases.english: And she would sit at the crossroads
and ask: The older one, what are his deeds?
He is an evil man who robs people.
The younger one, what are his deeds?
"A quiet man, dwelling in tents."
phrases.notes: בראשית 25:27

phrases.english: And she would cry,
until her eyelashes fell out.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָיְתָה יוֹשֶׁבֶת עַל פָּרָשַׁת דְּרָכִים וּמְשָׁאֶלֶת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes רב's story from Step 24 and shows why the weak eyes are praise.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Gives the righteous cause behind the weak eyes
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Weak eyes are a flaw that would be shameful to mention.
steps.terutzMaskana: Her eyes weakened from crying in prayer over marrying עשו. This is the prayer through which she got ahead of רחל.

steps.title: Linking לאה's crying to the פסוק 'Leah was hated'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא ties לאה's crying over עשו to the פסוק 'And ה׳ saw that Leah was hated' and asks what 'hated' means.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what the פסוק means: 'And ה׳ saw that Leah was hated.' What does 'hated' mean?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא connects the story of לאה crying to another פסוק and asks what the word 'hated' means there. This sets up the next move.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The story of לאה refusing עשו will be used to explain a hard word in the תורה. Before giving the answer, the גמרא first asks what 'שנואה' really means.

keyTerms.meaning: And this is what is written; it links a story to a פסוק

phrases.english: And this is what is written:
"And the Lord saw that Leah was hated"
phrases.notes: בראשית 29:31

phrases.english: What does "hated" mean?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the story of לאה's crying from Step 25 to explain a new פסוק.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The meaning of 'שנואה' in the פסוק about לאה.

steps.title: Rejecting the plain meaning of 'hated'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects reading 'hated' literally, because the תורה does not even speak shamefully about an impure animal.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say she was really hated, how could that be? The פסוק avoids shaming even an impure animal. Would it shame righteous people?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tests the plain meaning, that לאה was actually hated, and rejects it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the same argument used in Step 22 for 'רכות.' The תורה carefully avoids saying bad things even about animals. So it would surely not insult a צדקת like לאה.

keyTerms.meaning: If you say; it introduces a suggestion that will be rejected

phrases.english: If you say she was literally hated,
is that possible? About the shame of an impure animal
the verse did not speak,
would the verse speak about the shame of righteous people?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the most obvious answer to the question in Step 26.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The תורה avoids shaming even an impure animal, so it would not shame a righteous woman.

steps.title: לאה hated עשו's deeds, so God opened her womb
steps.stepSummary: 'Hated' means that the deeds of עשו were hated by לאה, and as a reward God gave her children.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, הקב"ה saw that the deeds of עשו were hateful to her, and so 'He opened her womb.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the true meaning: לאה was the one who hated, and what she hated was עשו's wicked behavior.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'שנואה' is moved from describing לאה to describing her feelings about עשו. This fits the end of the פסוק: because of her righteousness, God rewarded her with children.

keyTerms.meaning: The Holy One, Blessed be He

steps.whatToRemember: 'Leah was hated' means לאה hated עשו's wicked ways, and God rewarded her with children.

phrases.english: Rather, the Holy One, Blessed be He, saw
that the deeds of Esav were hateful in her eyes,
"and He opened her womb."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 26 after the plain meaning was rejected in Step 27.
steps.terutzMaskana: לאה hated עשו's deeds and was rewarded with children.

steps.title: What was רחל's modesty?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא turns to the second half of רבי יונתן's statement and asks what רחל's modesty was. It quotes the פסוק where יעקב tells רחל who he is.
steps.simpleTranslation: What was רחל's modesty? As it is written: 'And Jacob told Rachel that he was her father's brother, and that he was Rebecca's son.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now explains רחל's modesty, and it starts by quoting a פסוק that will need explaining.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יונתן said רחל had modesty (צניעות). The גמרא will build the story from this פסוק, and the next step points out a strange detail in it.

phrases.english: And what modesty did Rachel have?
As it is written:
"And Jacob told Rachel
that he was her father's brother,
and that he was Rebecca's son"
phrases.notes: בראשית 29:12

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves לאה and moves to the second part of רבי יונתן's statement, about רחל.

steps.title: יעקב was not really her father's brother
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא points out that יעקב was the son of לבן's sister, not לבן's brother.
steps.simpleTranslation: But he was the son of her father's sister!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the wording of the פסוק: יעקב was really רחל's cousin, so why call him her father's brother?
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבקה was לבן's sister, so יעקב was לבן's nephew. The word 'brother' therefore needs a deeper explanation.

keyTerms.meaning: But is it not so; it opens a challenge
The son of her father's sister

phrases.english: But he was the son of her father's sister!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the wording of the פסוק quoted in Step 29.
steps.kashyaTarget: The phrase 'אחי אביה' in the פסוק.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: יעקב was לבן's nephew, not his brother.

steps.title: יעקב and רחל's private conversation
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains with a conversation: יעקב asked רחל to marry him, and she warned him that לבן is a cheat who will not marry her off before her older sister.
steps.simpleTranslation: He asked her: Will you marry me? She said: Yes, but my father is a cheat and you cannot beat him. He asked: What is his trick? She said: I have an older sister, and he will not marry me off before her.
steps.whatsHappening: To answer the challenge, the גמרא tells the background conversation between יעקב and רחל. This sets up יעקב's reply in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רחל warns יעקב ahead of time about לבן's plan. Her warning explains why יעקב will describe himself as לבן's 'brother.'

phrases.english: Rather, he said to her:
Will you marry me?
She said to him: Yes,
but Father is a cheat,
and you cannot beat him.
He said to her: What is his trick?
She said to him:
I have a sister who is older than me,
and he will not marry me off before her.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins answering the challenge of Step 30 by telling the hidden conversation.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Background story that explains the פסוק

steps.title: יעקב: I am his brother in trickery
steps.stepSummary: יעקב answers that he is לבן's 'brother' in trickery, meaning his equal. That is what 'her father's brother' means.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to her: I am his brother in trickery.
steps.whatsHappening: This line finishes the answer: 'her father's brother' means יעקב is as clever as לבן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Brother' here does not describe family. It means an equal. יעקב was telling רחל that לבן would not be able to fool him.

keyTerms.meaning: I am his brother (his equal) in trickery

steps.confusionAlert: 'אחי אביה' is not about family relations here. It means יעקב matches לבן in cleverness.

phrases.english: He said to her: I am his brother in trickery.
phrases.notes: This is what the פסוק meant by 'her father's brother.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the answer begun in Step 31.

steps.title: רחל asks: may the righteous use trickery?
steps.stepSummary: רחל challenges יעקב: is a צדיק allowed to act with trickery?
steps.simpleTranslation: She said to him: Is it allowed for righteous people to act with trickery?
steps.whatsHappening: Inside the story, רחל questions whether trickery fits a righteous person like יעקב. This sets up his answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The issue is not whether יעקב is clever enough but whether it is proper. The next step answers with a פסוק.

phrases.english: She said to him:
And is it permitted for righteous people
to act with trickery?

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִי שְׁרֵי לְהוּ לְצַדִּיקֵי לְסַגּוֹיֵי בְּרַמָּאוּתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges יעקב's claim from Step 32 on moral grounds.
steps.kashyaTarget: יעקב's plan to match לבן's trickery.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A צדיק should not use deceit.

steps.title: With a crooked person, one may be clever; יעקב gives signs
steps.stepSummary: יעקב answers yes, quoting 'with the crooked You show Yourself twisty,' and gives רחל secret signs.
steps.simpleTranslation: Yes: 'With the pure You show Yourself pure, and with the crooked You show Yourself twisty.' He gave her signs.
steps.whatsHappening: יעקב proves from a פסוק that one may outsmart a crooked person, and then he acts on it by giving רחל secret signs.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק describes God acting toward people based on how they act. So against a cheat, outsmarting him is allowed. The signs would let יעקב know it was really רחל at the wedding.

phrases.english: Yes,
"With the pure You show Yourself pure,
and with the crooked You show Yourself twisty";
phrases.notes: שמואל ב 22:27

phrases.english: He gave her signs.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִין עִם נָבָר תִּתָּבָר וְעִם עִקֵּשׁ תִּתַּפָּל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רחל's challenge from Step 33.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A צדיק may never use trickery.
steps.terutzMaskana: Against a cheat, a צדיק may use cleverness.

steps.title: רחל gives the signs to לאה
steps.stepSummary: When לאה was brought in to the wedding, רחל gave her the signs so her sister would not be embarrassed.
steps.simpleTranslation: When they were bringing לאה in, רחל thought: Now my sister will be embarrassed. So she gave the signs to her.
steps.whatsHappening: This is רחל's act of modesty: she gave up her own protection so that לאה would not be shamed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The signs were meant to protect רחל from לבן's trick. Instead she quietly handed them to לאה, giving up her own wedding to save her sister from embarrassment.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the actual answer to 'what was רחל's modesty': she quietly gave up her own interest to protect her sister's dignity.

phrases.english: When they were bringing Leah in,
she thought:
phrases.notes: 'She' here is רחל.

phrases.english: Now my sister will be embarrassed.
She gave them to her.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the story: what happened to the signs from Step 34.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רחל gave her signs to לאה to spare her from shame. This was her modesty.

steps.title: 'In the morning, behold it was Leah' seems strange
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings the פסוק 'In the morning, behold it was Leah' and asks: was she not לאה before the morning?
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what is written: 'And it was in the morning, and behold, it was Leah.' Does that mean she was not לאה until now?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a פסוק that seems odd and asks a question about it. The story of the signs will explain it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'in the morning' suggest something changed overnight. Of course she was always לאה, so the פסוק needs an explanation.

keyTerms.meaning: And it was in the morning

phrases.english: And this is what is written:
"And it was in the morning, and behold, it was Leah"
phrases.notes: בראשית 29:25

phrases.english: Does that imply that until now
she was not Leah?!

steps.triggerLanguage: מִכְּלָל דְּעַד הַשְׁתָּא לָאו לֵאָה הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Connects the story of Step 35 to a פסוק and points out the difficulty in it.
steps.kashyaTarget: The words 'in the morning, behold it was Leah.'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: She was always לאה, so why say she became לאה only in the morning?

steps.title: Because of the signs, יעקב did not know until morning
steps.stepSummary: Since לאה had the signs that יעקב gave רחל, יעקב did not realize it was לאה until the morning.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, because of the signs that יעקב gave רחל, which she gave to לאה, he did not know it was her until that moment.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers: the פסוק means יעקב only discovered it was לאה in the morning, because she had the secret signs.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Without the signs, יעקב would have found out at once. רחל's quiet act is the reason he was fooled until morning, so the פסוק itself shows רחל's modesty.
steps.whatToRemember: רחל's modesty was giving her secret signs to לאה. That is why יעקב only realized 'in the morning' that it was לאה.

phrases.english: Rather, because of the signs
that Jacob gave to Rachel,
and she gave them to Leah,
he did not know it was her
until that moment.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא מִתּוֹךְ סִימָנִים שֶׁמָּסַר לָהּ יַעֲקֹב לְרָחֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the difficulty raised in Step 36.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reading the פסוק as being from יעקב's point of view
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The פסוק suggests she was not לאה before the morning.
steps.terutzMaskana: She was always לאה. יעקב only found out in the morning because of the signs.

steps.title: Seventy in the total, sixty-nine in the list
steps.stepSummary: אבא חליפא קרויא points out a contradiction. The total count of יעקב's family is seventy, but the names only add up to sixty-nine.
steps.simpleTranslation: אבא חליפא קרויא asked רבי חייא בר אבא: When the תורה gives the total, you find seventy. When it lists each person, you find seventy minus one!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new question about the family of יעקב. אבא חליפא קרויא notices that the total number given in the פסוק does not match the names in the list.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The total in the פסוק says seventy souls of יעקב's house came to מצרים. But when you add up the names one by one, you only get sixty-nine. He wants to know who the missing person is.

keyTerms.meaning: The reader (one who reads the תורה or פסוקים publicly)
In their total, the overall count
In their details, the list of names one by one

phrases.english: Abba Chalifa Karoya asked
phrases.notes: קרויא means 'the reader': someone who read פסוקים aloud for the people.

phrases.english: of Rabbi Chiyya bar Abba:
In their total, you find seventy;
phrases.notes: בראשית 46:27

phrases.aramaic: בִּפְרָטָן – אַתָּה מוֹצֵא שִׁבְעִים חָסֵר אֶחָד!
phrases.english: in their individual listing, you find seventy less one!

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּעָא מִינֵּיהּ אַבָּא חֲלִיפָא קִרְוָיָא מֵרַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic within the discussion of יעקב's family. It no longer deals with the signs between רחל and לאה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The פסוק's total of seventy people who went down to מצרים
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The total and the list of names contradict each other, because the list only adds up to sixty-nine.

steps.title: A twin sister was born with דינה
steps.stepSummary: רבי חייא בר אבא answers that a twin sister was born with דינה. She is the seventieth person, and he hints to her from the word ואת.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: A twin sister was born with דינה, as it is written: 'and [את] דינה his daughter.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי חייא בר אבא solves the missing-person problem. He says דינה had a twin sister who is counted in the total but not named in the list.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word את in 'ואת דינה בתו' is read as adding someone extra. That extra person is a twin sister of דינה, and she brings the count up to seventy.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And [את]': a little word here read as hinting to one more person

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: תְּאוֹמָה הָיְתָה עִם דִּינָה,
phrases.english: He said to him: A twin sister was born with Dinah,
as it is written: "And [et] Dinah his daughter."
phrases.notes: בראשית 46:15. The extra word את is read as pointing to one more person besides דינה.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: תְּאוֹמָה הָיְתָה עִם דִּינָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in step 38.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Finds the missing person hinted to in the wording of the פסוק
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The list of names seems to have only sixty-nine people.
steps.terutzMaskana: An unnamed twin sister of דינה, hinted to by the word את, is the seventieth person.

steps.title: Then בנימין would also need a twin
steps.stepSummary: אבא חליפא challenges the answer. If the word את means an extra twin, then a similar פסוק about בנימין would mean he had a twin too, and the count would go over seventy.
steps.simpleTranslation: But if that is so, a twin sister was also born with בנימין, as it is written:
steps.whatsHappening: אבא חליפא begins to challenge the answer about דינה's twin. He says the same reasoning would give בנימין a twin as well, and he starts to quote a פסוק. The quote continues in the next part of the text.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If an את in a פסוק adds a twin, then any similar את about בנימין would add another person. That would make the total seventy-one instead of seventy. So the method used in step 39 seems to prove too much.

keyTerms.meaning: But if so: if your reasoning is right, then...
בנימין, the youngest son of יעקב

phrases.english: But if that is so,
a twin sister was born with Benjamin,
as it is written:

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא מֵעַתָּה, תְּאוֹמָה הָיְתָה עִם בִּנְיָמִן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the method of reading in step 39.
steps.kashyaTarget: Using the word את to find an extra twin
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The same method would also give בנימין a twin, and then the total would be more than seventy.
